html:
Tel Aviv was founded in April 1909 by Jewish families who drew lots for plots on sand dunes north of the old Arab port of Jaffa. It was planned as a garden suburb, and became the first modern Hebrew-speaking city.

Its name, from a book by Theodor Herzl translated into Hebrew, means hill of spring. It grew fast with immigration under the British mandate, and in the 1930s architects trained in Germany built thousands of white buildings in the Bauhaus style; the White City is a World Heritage Site.

David Ben-Gurion declared the State of Israel in Tel Aviv on 14 May 1948. Jaffa was joined to it in 1950. It is the centre of Israel's business and tech industry, with its beaches and nightlife.
